title: HUSTLR Pickleball & Social Club / CYS Architect Sdn Bhd
text:
HUSTLR Pickleball & Social Club / CYS Architect Sdn Bhd

An abandoned food court in Taman Taynton View, Cheras, has been transformed into Hustlr Pickleball & Social Club — a new sports and social destination that adapts an existing steel structure while introducing a distinctive identity and a new layer of community life. What can an underutilized building become when its potential is reconsidered? For Hustlr, the answer was not to start again, but to work with what was already there. Inspired by the client's passion for pickleball, the vision extended beyond creating a place to play.

title: Vanguard House / Ming Architects
text:
Vanguard House / Ming Architects

Vanguard House is a spacious residence with privacy and serenity at the forefront of its design. With concealed living spaces and the incorporation of water features at its core, it creates a light and relaxing atmosphere complemented by its use of materials.

title: Sona Listening Practices / Épico Studio
text:
Sona Listening Practices / Épico Studio

Sona is a space dedicated to listening practices, designed by Épico Estudio and Panorama. Located in the heart of Mexico City, in the Condesa neighborhood, the 245 m² venue—spearheaded by a group of friends led by Luis López (Lulo)—is defined as an environment oriented toward sonic immersion: device-free, alcohol-free, and distraction-free. The concept transforms the act of listening into a conscious, deliberate, shared, and, above all, deeply sensory experience.

title: Minthis Resort Development / Woods Bagot
text:
Minthis Resort Development / Woods Bagot

Minthis is a resort-style development located in the hillside setting of Tsada Village in Paphos. With Cypriot developer Pafilia, Woods Bagot's London studio delivered master planning, architecture, interior design, and branding services to create a unique retreat-style experience, combining the best of local antiquity and premium amenities.

title: LAND OVER WATER / FIRM architects
text:
LAND OVER WATER / FIRM architects

In Hoofddorp, the transformation of a 1990s office building into a contemporary workplace for APPM translates the Dutch landscape into an architectural language of water, clay, and vegetation, bringing together sustainability, spatial identity, and new ways of working.

title: Maryland House / Remi C.T.
text:
Maryland House / Remi C.T.

A bold example of infill housing architecture, Maryland House redefines urban living through spatial innovation and design precision. It is a dwelling that challenges traditional spatial hierarchy in the home to focus on the reality of modern city living.

title: Art, Architecture, Archaeology: A Refuge for Artists at Amman’s Darat al Funun
text:
Art, Architecture, Archaeology: A Refuge for Artists at Amman’s Darat al Funun

At a time when public support for the arts is under pressure in many countries, Darat al Funun — literally "House of the Arts" — stands by its long-standing mission to champion artists. "Artists are witnesses of their time," affirms Suha Shoman, its founder. "Maybe Art does not operate change, but it does record it […] it points fingers. At the same time, it speaks of, even if it's so difficult and at times so violent, it speaks of beauty as well."

title: Vandeuren III-IV / P&P Architectes + Atelier d'Architecture A4
text:
Vandeuren III-IV / P&P Architectes + Atelier d'Architecture A4

Winner of the Be-Exemplary Award 2019, Vandeuren III and IV is part of an ambitious renovation strategy for social housing in Brussels. The project transforms 160 dwellings into 132 reconfigured units while integrating shared facilities and a reorganization of outdoor spaces. The intervention combines heritage preservation, quality of use, and circularity, enhancing the existing fabric while responding to contemporary needs.

title: Minou-On Apartment Renovation / CROSSARCHITECTURE / Mehrdad Makaremi
text:
Minou-On Apartment Renovation / CROSSARCHITECTURE / Mehrdad Makaremi

In Minou-On Apartment, a thirty-year-old duplex in Tehran gains a villa-like quality as a former terrace becomes a skylit, planted void. A timber system connects the home's two floors, working with the exposed concrete frame to reorganize rooms, circulation, and everyday life.

title: Itchimbía Housing / Mejía Narváez Arquitectos
text:
Itchimbía Housing / Mejía Narváez Arquitectos

Itchimbía transforms a void in Quito's Historic Center into six homes that reveal the city through a gradual journey, where material and light make the passage of time perceptible.

title: FM House / Dado Castello Branco Arquitetura
text:
FM House / Dado Castello Branco Arquitetura

"Incorporating such a complete program on a limited plot of land was a real challenge," says Dado Castello Branco.

title: Bachour Café / Estudio Guto Requena
text:
Bachour Café / Estudio Guto Requena

The architectural project draws inspiration from French boulevards and the aesthetic richness of Brazilian design, exploring contrasts between opulence and warmth, tradition and innovation, craft and technology. The concept incorporates references to Art Nouveau — a movement that emerged in Paris during the Belle Époque at the end of the 19th century, a period of great cultural effervescence marked by organic lines, fluid forms, and natural inspiration. These elements are reinterpreted in the design, creating a composition that blends tropicality and technology.

Pavilion in the Oaks / Mork-Ulnes Architects

The clients approached Mork-Ulnes Architects with a desire for a flexible space that could provide a meditative, spa-like experience for exercise, yoga, and quiet contemplation, as well as a place for social gatherings with their extended family and friends.

title: Kerena Funeral Services / MYT+GLVDK
text:
Kerena Funeral Services / MYT+GLVDK

title: Neuweilerstrasse Development / Volpatohatz
text:
Neuweilerstrasse Development / Volpatohatz

VOLPATOHATZ won a competition for the design of an apartment building in Basel, Switzerland. The competition proposal, juried by architect and professor Harry Gugger, includes seven apartments over five levels, plus a basement for bikes, plants, and storage.

title: Argyle House: The Story Behind Edinburgh’s Brutalist Landmark
text:
Argyle House: The Story Behind Edinburgh’s Brutalist Landmark

Rising from the rocks that form the base of Castle Rock in Edinburgh, Argyle House stands in stark contrast to the city's most iconic landmark. Built in the late 1960s, this angular, grey building is a quintessential example of post-war Brutalist architecture. A geometric concrete structure stripped of ornamentation that has recently become an unlikely star on screen, serving as the backdrop for the series Dept. Q, based on novels by Danish author Jussi Adler-Olsen. Yet the 11-story complex, which once housed government offices and now homes promising startups, continues to divide opinion. On one hand, its imposing presence challenges the historic urban fabric; on the other, its architectural significance makes it an important part of the city's modern heritage.

title: Capsule Retreat / East Architecture Studio
text:
Capsule Retreat / East Architecture Studio

Overlooking the coniferous forests of Mount Lebanon, Capsule Retreat is a modern home that beds into an ancient landscape of sandstone outcrops and alpine villages. Paying close attention to the flesh of the site, the design process sets aside aesthetic sensitivities in favor of a more physiological reading, one that acknowledges the stratification embedded in its materiality, where incompleteness and low-tech building technologies found in rural settings were the starting point to weave in design practice as context.

title: JSWD Wins Competition to Design Mixed-Use RIYMAR Towers in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
text:
JSWD Wins Competition to Design Mixed-Use RIYMAR Towers in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

German architecture practice JSWD has been selected to design RIYMAR Towers, a proposed mixed-use development in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, following an international invited architecture competition organized by Malcolm Reading Consultants on behalf of RIYMAR Real Estate. Located near the intersection of King Fahd Road and Olaya Street, adjacent to the Riyadh Gallery complex, the project is planned as a new development combining residential, hospitality, office, retail, and leisure functions. The project is positioned within the broader urban transformation outlined by Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030, which includes objectives related to tourism, cultural development, hospitality, and increased homeownership.

title: Maison de l'Environnement et de la Biodiversité / Bulle, Poirier & Justman Architectes
text:
Maison de l'Environnement et de la Biodiversité / Bulle, Poirier & Justman Architectes

On the edge of a municipal estate in Mitry-Mory, between farmland and the town center, the Maison de l'Environnement et de la Biodiversité occupies a former go-kart track, framed by grassy embankments and already reclaimed by a beekeepers' association and its hives. Next to the communal restaurant and the archery range, the city wished to create a community venue dedicated to environmental education: a multipurpose hall, a honey house, and a covered terrace, within a compact footprint of 225 m².

title: SHAU’s Microlibraries Initiative Expands with a New Project in Jakarta
text:
SHAU’s Microlibraries Initiative Expands with a New Project in Jakarta

A new microlibrary project by Indonesian studio SHAU is under construction in Jakarta. The Microlibrary Taman Puring is part of the microlibraries initiative designed and organized by SHAU Rotterdam-Bandung (Florian Heinzelmann and Daliana Suryawinata), in collaboration with the City of Jakarta and the Microlibrary Foundation, a nonprofit initiative dedicated to expanding a network of sustainable, multifunctional community reading spaces across low-income neighborhoods in Indonesia. SHAU's first project, Kampung Mrican Phase 1, received the highest prize in the social architecture category of the Ammodo Architecture Award 2025, funding that made possible the realization of this second one.

title: What Architecture Brings Together: Encounters at Open House Valencia 2026
text:
What Architecture Brings Together: Encounters at Open House Valencia 2026

Architectural mediation is also a form of spatial and urban production. Open House Valencia offers a way of understanding it as a relational practice capable of introducing new dynamics into the everyday structure of the city. Its urban dimension takes shape through a temporary infrastructure that redistributes attention, access and urban rhythms, bringing together spaces that usually remain outside the scope of shared experience.

title: Casa Tranquilo / DADO
text:
Casa Tranquilo / DADO

Casa Tranquilo is a 10,000 sq. ft. villa in Verla Canca, North Goa, set within dense forest. Our inspiration was not a building or a style but a philosophy of slow living: a home where the day is marked by birdsong and the changing light through the trees. We let the existing forest guide the design, so that every tree that could be saved was woven into the plan and the house feels like it grew from the forest floor rather than being built on top of it.

title: LYNK&CO Motorsport Experience Center Chengdu / MUDA-Architects
text:
LYNK&CO Motorsport Experience Center Chengdu / MUDA-Architects

Translating the language of automotive performance into architectural space forms the starting point of the LYNK & CO Motorsport Experience Center (MEC). Located at the heart of Tianfu International Circuit in Chengdu Eastern New Area, adjacent to the main grandstand, the project forms part of Geely's Mintimes Spaceport development.
